items.symptoms: I have a lot of itchy spots on my skin. They're sometimes red or bumpy, and sometimes they're different colors than the rest of my skin. I also get these weird bumps that look like little balls.
items.title: Distinguish Fungal Morphology from Allergic Hives
items.when: When differentiating between allergic reactions and fungal infections based on skin lesion descriptions.
items.cue: Allergic reactions typically present as transient, uniform wheals or hives, whereas fungal infections often present as persistent, discrete nodules or 'ball-like' bumps with potential color variation.

items.symptoms: I have been having a fever for a few days and now I have sores near my nose. The sores are painful and I feel uncomfortable.
items.title: Distinguish Localized Bacterial Sores from Systemic Viral Exanthems
items.when: When a patient presents with fever and skin lesions, particularly when the lesions are localized to a specific area (e.g., face/nose) rather than widespread.
items.cue: Localized, painful, crusted sores near the nose or mouth with fever suggest impetigo (bacterial), whereas widespread, itchy, vesicular lesions across the body suggest chicken pox (viral).

items.symptoms: I have developed rashes all over my body that are itchy and I have lost my appetite. I feel very tired all day and I feel like something is wrong with my body.
items.title: Distinguishing Dengue from Chickenpox by Rash Morphology and Systemic Severity
items.when: When a patient presents with a widespread itchy rash accompanied by significant systemic symptoms like fatigue and loss of appetite, and the classifier must choose between chickenpox and dengue.
items.cue: Dengue is characterized by a maculopapular rash often accompanied by high fever, severe myalgia/arthralgia ('breakbone fever'), and thrombocytopenia, whereas chickenpox presents with a vesicular rash in various stages of development and typically milder systemic symptoms.

items.symptoms: I've been coughing a lot, and I'm really tired. I have a fever, and it's hard to breathe. I also cough up a lot of mucous.
items.title: Distinguishing Infectious vs. Obstructive Respiratory Patterns
items.when: When a patient presents with dyspnea and cough, but the classifier must choose between an infectious process (like pneumonia) and an obstructive/inflammatory airway disease (like asthma).
items.cue: High fever and purulent sputum strongly indicate an infectious etiology like pneumonia, whereas dyspnea with clear or scant mucus and absence of high fever points toward obstructive conditions like bronchial asthma.

items.symptoms: I have red, itchy bumps all over my body. They're especially bad on my arms and legs. I also have a headache and a fever. I don't feel like eating anything and have lost my appetite.
items.title: Itchiness as a Primary Differentiator
items.when: When distinguishing between viral exanthems (like Dengue) and vesicular viral infections (like Chickenpox) in patients with fever and rash.
items.cue: Intense pruritus (itching) is a hallmark of Chickenpox, whereas Dengue rashes are typically non-pruritic or only mildly itchy, making severe itchiness a strong indicator against Dengue.

items.symptoms: I have a rash on my skin that is red, raised, and filled with fluid. It is painful to touch and I have a fever.
items.title: Pain vs. Itch in Vesicular Rashes
items.when: When distinguishing between bacterial skin infections (like impetigo) and viral exanthems (like chickenpox) presenting with fluid-filled blisters.
items.cue: Painful, tender vesicles or pustules typically indicate a bacterial infection like impetigo, whereas intensely itchy vesicles are the hallmark of viral conditions like chickenpox.

items.symptoms: I have a rash on my face and near my nose. It's been there for a few days and it's starting to spread down my arms and legs.
items.title: Prioritize Localized Origin Over Spread
items.when: When a rash begins as a localized lesion on the face (especially near the nose) and subsequently spreads to extremities.
items.cue: A rash originating as a localized bacterial sore near the nose indicates impetigo, whereas chicken pox typically presents with a widespread, systemic viral exanthem from the onset.

items.symptoms: I have a high fever, chills, nausea, and severe itching. I also have a headache and am sweating a lot. I have muscle aches and nausea.
items.title: Prioritize Cyclical Fever Patterns Over Itching
items.when: When a patient presents with high fever, chills, and sweating alongside itching, and the classifier must distinguish between a viral exanthem (like chickenpox) and a parasitic infection (like malaria).
items.cue: The presence of distinct cyclical episodes of chills followed by high fever and profuse sweating is a stronger indicator of malaria than itching is for chickenpox, especially when the rash is not explicitly described as vesicular or crusted.

items.symptoms: I have rashes on my chest and back and I itch all over my body. I sometimes have flaky skin, which often leaves marks on my body.
items.title: Distinguish Drug Reaction from Psoriasis by Distribution and Morphology
items.when: When a patient presents with generalized itching and skin lesions that are described as 'flaky' or 'scaly' but lack the classic well-demarcated, thick silvery plaques of psoriasis, especially if the distribution is widespread (trunk and extremities) rather than localized to extensor surfaces.
items.cue: Drug reactions often present with widespread, symmetric, pruritic rashes that may be maculopapular or exfoliative (flaky) without the distinct, thick, silvery scale and well-defined borders characteristic of psoriatic plaques.

items.symptoms: I have been experiencing a lot of belly pain and constipation. I also feel like I need to vomit, and I am feeling very weak.
items.title: Constipation vs. Diarrhea in Typhoid vs. Peptic Ulcer
items.when: When distinguishing between typhoid and peptic ulcer disease in patients presenting with abdominal pain and nausea.
items.cue: Constipation is a key differentiator for typhoid (especially in early stages or specific presentations), whereas peptic ulcer disease is primarily characterized by meal-related epigastric pain and rarely presents with constipation as a primary symptom.

items.symptoms: I've been having trouble breathing, coughing a lot, and feeling exhausted. I have a fever and have been coughing up a lot of thick, sticky mucus. I'm just so tired and worn out from dealing with this.
items.title: Distinguishing Asthma from Pneumonia via Sputum and Fever
items.when: When a patient presents with respiratory distress, cough, and fatigue, but the presence of high fever and thick, purulent sputum is reported.
items.cue: High fever combined with thick, purulent sputum strongly indicates an infectious etiology like pneumonia, whereas bronchial asthma typically presents with clear or scant mucus and lacks high fever.

items.symptoms: I've been feeling really sick lately. I've been having a lot of nausea and vomiting, and I've lost my appetite. I've also been feeling really weak.
items.title: Prioritize Systemic Signs Over Local GI Symptoms
items.when: When a patient presents with non-specific gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, anorexia, weakness) without explicit mention of localized abdominal pain or specific bowel habits.
items.cue: The absence of localized abdominal pain and the presence of profound systemic weakness should lower the confidence in localized structural GI disorders like peptic ulcer disease, keeping systemic infections like typhoid in the differential despite the lack of explicit fever mention in the initial summary.

items.symptoms: I have small red bumps on my arms and face. They are itchy and make my day very uncomfortable.
items.title: Prioritize Viral Prodrome and Evolution over Static Itch
items.when: When distinguishing between allergic dermatitis and viral exanthems (like chickenpox) presenting with pruritic papules.
items.cue: Chickenpox is distinguished by the presence of systemic prodromal symptoms (fever, malaise) and the characteristic evolution of lesions through multiple stages (macules to crusts) simultaneously, whereas allergies typically present as static, localized urticaria or eczema without systemic involvement.

items.symptoms: I have a stuffy nose and nasal congestion. I sometimes have a stiff neck and chest discomfort at night. I can't taste or smell anything.
items.title: Distinguishing Allergy from Cold via Symptom Duration and Systemic Signs
items.when: When a patient presents with nasal congestion and loss of smell/taste, but lacks fever, body aches, or sore throat, and reports chronic or recurrent symptoms.
items.cue: Allergies typically present with isolated nasal symptoms (congestion, anosmia) and potential musculoskeletal discomfort from chronic mouth breathing or sinus pressure, whereas common colds are acute viral infections characterized by systemic symptoms like fever, myalgia, and sore throat alongside nasal issues.

items.symptoms: I have a rash all over my body and I feel really itchy. I'm also feeling really tired and I don't have an appetite.
items.title: Itch Intensity as a Differentiator
items.when: When distinguishing between viral exanthems (like Dengue) and vesicular diseases (like Chickenpox) in patients presenting with widespread rash, fatigue, and anorexia.
items.cue: Significant, intense pruritus (itching) is a hallmark of Chickenpox, whereas Dengue rashes are typically maculopapular and less intensely pruritic, often accompanied by high fever and severe myalgia.
